---
title: "From RSEM files to z-scores against controls"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This page goes from a folder of RSEM files to values ready for plots, one pipe at a time. The folder
holds one `*.genes.results` file per sample (and, for the last section, the `*.isoforms.results`
files), and a sample table names the groups:

```text
rsem/                     metadata.csv
  CTRL_1.genes.results      sample_id,ref,group
  CTRL_2.genes.results      CTRL_1,CTRL_1.genes.results,control
  DRUG_1.genes.results      CTRL_2,CTRL_2.genes.results,control
  DRUG_2.genes.results      DRUG_1,DRUG_1.genes.results,drug
                            DRUG_2,DRUG_2.genes.results,drug
```

## 1. Check, then read

```{r}
library(rsemverse)
rsem_check("rsem")                                   # every problem in the files, all at once
tpm <- rsem_read("rsem", "metadata.csv", species = "human", expr = "tpm")
```

`rsem_check()` stops nothing; it lists. `rsem_read()` stops on the same errors (a missing file, genes
in another order, a different set of transcripts for a gene). With `metadata = NULL` it finds the files
and names the samples after them.

## 2. Look at the effective lengths before tximport or DESeq2

```{r}
len <- rsem_read("rsem", "metadata.csv", species = "human", expr = "length")
attr(len, "zero_length")                             # genes with length 0, per sample
rsem_length_profile(len) |> subset(zero_fraction > 0 & zero_fraction < 1)
```

Genes with length 0 in some samples are the ones that stop `DESeqDataSetFromTximport()`. Removing them
(`rsem_as_tximport(zero_length = "drop")`) or importing transcript-level files avoids changing their
length offset.

## 3. Choose a detection threshold

```{r}
tpm |> rsem_detection_curve(thresholds = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5), min_samples = c(1, 0.5))
filtered <- tpm |> rsem_filter(min_value = 1, min_samples = 0.5)
```

Each row of the curve is the number of genes `rsem_filter()` keeps with those settings. Neither call
needs `expr = "tpm"`: the table from `rsem_read()` knows what it holds.

## 4. Remove rRNA and see the gene-type composition

```{r}
gtf <- "gencode.v29.annotation.gtf.gz"               # the annotation the RSEM reference was built from
tpm |> rsem_biotype_profile(gtf, types = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "rRNA", "Mt_rRNA"))
filtered <- filtered |> rsem_subset(remove = c("rrna", "mito_rrna"), annotation = gtf)
```

## 5. Z-scores against the controls

```{r}
ref <- filtered |> rsem_fit_reference("control", metadata = "metadata.csv", group = "group")
z   <- filtered |> rsem_apply_reference(ref, zero_sd = "drop")
rsem_steps(z)                                        # what was done, in order
```

`ref` keeps the control means and standard deviations on the `log2(TPM + 1)` scale. A later batch on the
same scale is scored against the same controls with `rsem_apply_reference(new_tpm, ref)`.

## 6. Plot or share

```{r}
long <- z |> rsem_long("metadata.csv")
ggplot2::ggplot(subset(long, gene == "CDKN1A"), ggplot2::aes(group, value)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() + ggplot2::labs(y = "z-score against controls")

tpm |> rsem_write("tpm.tsv.gz", annotation = gtf)    # gene, gene IDs, gene type, samples
tpm |> rsem_write("tpm.gct", format = "gct")         # for GSEA and ssGSEA
```

## 7. Transcripts

```{r}
iso  <- rsem_read("rsem", "metadata.csv", species = "human", expr = "tpm", level = "isoform")
main <- iso |> rsem_select_isoforms(min_tpm = 1, min_fraction = 0.1, rule = "all")
iso |> rsem_isoform_usage()                          # dominant share and entropy per gene and sample
```

The selected values are the original estimates; to quantify against the selection, build a new reference
and rerun RSEM.
